post.instagram:
Send this to the parent who is tired of being the bad guy about screen time.

Screen time tends to get taken, not given. You never quite decided, and you never quite said yes. So every evening turns into a fresh negotiation, and you are the one who has to end it.

We stopped negotiating about screen time. We wrote down the price instead.

That is Family Quests:

1. You set real jobs. A packed school bag, an hour outside, helping with dinner.
2. Your child ticks them off on their own page, and you agree each one.
3. Every job pays stars, and stars become minutes at a rate you set.
4. Bedtime, mealtimes and school hours are not for sale at any price.
5. The minutes run on a timer you can both see.

When the time runs out, it is the deal ending, not you being mean.

What is the screen time argument you have most often at your house?

What stage is your child? Three questions, no sign up, link in bio.
